# daily { #wdm.daily }

`daily`

The morning routine's bookkeeping: record today's readings, keep a plan log.

``wdm daily`` is the whole daily obligation in one command (see
`wdm.cli.cmd_daily`). This module holds the parts of it that touch files,
kept apart so they can be tested without running the filter:

* `record` writes values into a day's row of the observations CSV:
  this morning's weigh-in and waist, or yesterday's food, creating the row if
  needed. Row ``k`` holds the morning readings of day ``k`` and the food eaten
  that day, so entering the weight first thing is exactly right; the food
  columns are filled in tomorrow.
* `log_plan` archives every plan with the facts needed to reproduce it,
  which a plain ``plan.csv``, overwritten daily, cannot do.

The CSV is edited through the ``csv`` module with every cell kept as the string
it was, so nothing is reformatted: a line that was not touched is byte-for-byte
what it was.

## Functions

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [add_column](#wdm.daily.add_column) | Add an empty column ``col`` (before ``before`` if present); ``False`` if it exists. |
| [ask_number](#wdm.daily.ask_number) | Prompt until the answer is a number or blank (``None``). |
| [day_has_food](#wdm.daily.day_has_food) | Whether ``date``'s row has an energy total or a full macro split. |
| [day_totals](#wdm.daily.day_totals) | The day's logged totals for the prescribed quantities, zero where blank. |
| [day_value](#wdm.daily.day_value) | The raw cell for ``col`` on ``date``, or ``None`` if the row or cell is empty. |
| [last_weight_lb](#wdm.daily.last_weight_lb) | The most recent weigh-in in the file, or ``None`` if there is none. |
| [log_plan](#wdm.daily.log_plan) | Archive ``plan`` as ``<start>.csv`` and append a row to ``log.csv``. |
| [prescription](#wdm.daily.prescription) | Today's prescription: the latest logged plan that starts on ``date``. |
| [record](#wdm.daily.record) | Write ``values`` into ``date``'s row; return what was done. |
| [record_morning](#wdm.daily.record_morning) | Write this morning's readings into ``date``'s row; return what was done. |

### add_column { #wdm.daily.add_column }

```python
daily.add_column(path, col, *, before='notes')
```

Add an empty column ``col`` (before ``before`` if present); ``False`` if it exists.

Every row gets an empty cell, so the file stays rectangular and nothing
else in it changes.

### ask_number { #wdm.daily.ask_number }

```python
daily.ask_number(prompt, ask=input)
```

Prompt until the answer is a number or blank (``None``).

### day_has_food { #wdm.daily.day_has_food }

```python
daily.day_has_food(path, date)
```

Whether ``date``'s row has an energy total or a full macro split.

``None`` when there is no row for that date at all.

### day_totals { #wdm.daily.day_totals }

```python
daily.day_totals(path, date)
```

The day's logged totals for the prescribed quantities, zero where blank.

### day_value { #wdm.daily.day_value }

```python
daily.day_value(path, date, col)
```

The raw cell for ``col`` on ``date``, or ``None`` if the row or cell is empty.

### last_weight_lb { #wdm.daily.last_weight_lb }

```python
daily.last_weight_lb(path)
```

The most recent weigh-in in the file, or ``None`` if there is none.

### log_plan { #wdm.daily.log_plan }

```python
daily.log_plan(
    log_dir,
    plan,
    *,
    write_plan_csv,
    target_weight_lb,
    target_date,
    trend_lb,
    maintenance_kcal,
    constraints_ok,
    command,
)
```

Archive ``plan`` as ``<start>.csv`` and append a row to ``log.csv``.

A replan on the same day overwrites that day's archived plan but adds a
new log row, so the log records every prescription ever issued.

### prescription { #wdm.daily.prescription }

```python
daily.prescription(log_dir, date)
```

Today's prescription: the latest logged plan that starts on ``date``.

### record { #wdm.daily.record }

```python
daily.record(path, date, values, *, add=False, replace=False)
```

Write ``values`` into ``date``'s row; return what was done.

An existing row keeps its episode and gets the values in its empty cells;
a value that would overwrite a different one is refused, since a silent
overwrite is how a typo becomes data. With ``add``, values are summed into
what is there instead: that is how a meal joins the day's food totals. With
``replace``, a new value overwrites the old one, for running totals such as
a step count. A
missing row is appended to the most recent episode, so a new diet attempt
still needs its first row by hand. ``None`` values are skipped.

### record_morning { #wdm.daily.record_morning }

```python
daily.record_morning(path, date, *, weight_lb=None, waist_in=None)
```

Write this morning's readings into ``date``'s row; return what was done.
